Appeal No. 4422 of 2024

National Insurance Company
 Versus
 Bewa Mithilesh Tiwari And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Anjali Banerjee - Senior Advocate with Ms. Shail Patel
 the appellant/Insurance Company.
Shri A.S. Parihar- Advocate for the respondent/Claimants.
Shri Sanjay Gupta - Advocate for the respondents No.7 & 8.
Shri A.N. Sharma - Advocate for the respondent No.9.

Order 
Record is received.
Heard on admission.
The appeal is admitted for final hearing.
2. Heard on I.A. No.11470/2024 an application for condonation of delay of 2 days in preferring appeal.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, I.A. No. 11470/2024 is allowed.
Delay of 2 days is condoned.
3. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, case is admitted for hearing.
The appeal is finally heard and is disposed of as below.

4. This appeal has been filed under Section 173 (1) of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17188 2 MA-4422-2024 Mother Vehicle Act, 1988 by the appellant/Insurance Company

being aggrieved with the award dated 29.02.2024 passed in Claim Case No.813/2018 (Widow Mithilesh Tiwari W/o Satendra Kumar Tiwari (died) Vs. Ajay Kumar Patel and others) by National Insurance Company vs Bewa Mithilesh Tiwari on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120624442/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 the learned MACT, Rewa (for short 'Tribunal') whereby for the death of deceased- Satendra Kumar son of Tulsi Prasad Tiwari who was aged 41 years at the time of motor accident dated 30.08.2018,
has awarded compensation of Rs.18,55,500/-.
5.

It is seen that learned tribunal held that breach of Insurance Company is not proved, but in the light of issue No. 4 which is to the effect that whether on the date of the motor accident, the motorcycle bearing No. MP19-MS7956 was insured with the non-applicant No.3 (Bajaj Alliance Insurance Com. Ltd).

It has also held that it was not insured with Bajaj Alliance Insurance Com.
Ltd., but without framing a formal question in this regard has held that it was insured with the non- applicant No.4 (National Insurance Co. Ltd.) which was impleaded subsequently on 11.08.2023 in the claim petition filed on 01.11.2018.

Therefore, appellant/Insurance Company is seeking to set aside the award dated 29.02.2024.
6.

At the time of arguments, it was submitted by learned senior counsel for the appellant that Ex.
D/8 (Policy) was a fake policy, therefore, no relief could have been given on other hand.

7. Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that as per the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17188 3 MA-4422-2024 judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., (2018) 5 SSC 656 "pay and recover" order should be made and they also submitted that on the basis of pleadings of evidence and in the fact and circumstances of the case, liability on the National Insurance company has been rightly fixed.
8.

entities.text: Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., (2018) 5 SSC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considered the arguments and perused the record.
The question arises for consideration before this Court is whether interference can be made in award of the Tribunal by this Court.
It seen that judgment of Mangla Ram (supra) in Paras 35 & 36 was regarding ante-dated cover note and not a fake cover note.

It is further seen that the learned Claims Tribunal in Para 18 of its award has held thus:-
"    ,                 
       ,           
 ,        19 /7956   30.08.2018    4               "
9.
Now, there is finding of the learned Tribunal that on the basis of evidence of all parties, forged policy and some wrong document have been issued.
Hence, when this fact is considered, then this court has a genuine doubt as to whether Tribunal had tried to get into the bottom of the controversy and make a proper inquiry in this regard.

Therefore, with a view not to do injustice with any party,
remand of case would be required.

10. Therefore, award dated 29.02.204 is set aside, and case is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17188 4 MA-4422-2024 remanded back to the learned Tribunal to give an additional opportunity of hearing to all parties.

If required, to call any person or authority as a court witness along with documents and to record the evidence, and if anyone wants to bring additional National Insurance Company vs Bewa Mithilesh Tiwari on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120624442/
2 evidence, then permission is also to be granted and opportunities be given to all the parties.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Tribunal shall decide the claim afresh as per law.
11. With the aforesaid observation, the Misc. Appeal is disposed of.
Parties are directed to appear before the concerned Tribunal on 05.05.2025.
